text:
If you've got outdoor plans today, front-load them: mornings are the calm before a genuinely wet stretch moves in. We're starting clear and mild, but showers and thunderstorms build in by early afternoon, with a high near 85. The Euro is much wetter than the American model here (near 100% chance versus 60%) and even the sunnier read keeps the sky unsettled, so I'd trust the forecasters' own call of 80% and plan around scattered downpours from midday on, some potentially heavy.

Tonight is when it gets serious: rain becomes steady and widespread, 90% coverage, with isolated flash flooding possible if storms stall over the same spot, mainly south of us. Wednesday stays cloudy and showery with a high only near 77, and the wet pattern holds into Wednesday night. On the lake, winds stay light out of the south early, but afternoon storms mean you want to be off the broad waters well before that early-afternoon window, and the air's just moderate today from lingering smoke, not a big deal for most. Bottom line: enjoy the morning, but plan any lake time or long outdoor stretch before 1pm, because the rest of the day through Wednesday is a wash.

NWS FORECAST:
  Today: A chance of showers and thunderstorms between 1pm and 4pm, then showers and thunderstorms. Partly sunny, with a high near 85. South wind around 9 mph. Chance of precipitation is 80%. New rainfall amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.
  Tonight: Showers and thunderstorms. Cloudy, with a low around 66. Southeast wind around 8 mph, with gusts as high as 24 mph. Chance of precipitation is 90%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.
  Wednesday: Rain showers before noon, then showers and thunderstorms likely. Cloudy, with a high near 77. East wind around 7 mph. Chance of precipitation is 80%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.
  Wednesday Night: Showers and thunderstorms likely. Cloudy, with a low around 63. Northeast wind around 6 mph. Chance of precipitation is 60%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.
AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-07-28T11:12:00+00:00):
  1. Numerous showers and thunderstorms today with localized heavy rain.
  2. Periods of rain continue tonight through Wednesday night. Isolated flash flooding is possible if storms repeatedly track over the same area.
  3. Unsettled weather continues into the weekend with the approach of another developing mid to upper level trough.
AFD WHAT CHANGED: As of 217 AM EDT Tuesday... The forecast remains on track. Rainfall amounts have been refined with the latest guidance, but no significant changes to the overall forecast messaging. Highest rainfall totals still expected over northern NY and southern VT today through Wednesday night. Some isolated flash flooding remains possible, mainly tonight into Wednesday, but widespread hydro issues are not anticipated at this point.
LAKE (broad waters):
  Today: South winds 10 to 15 knots. Showers with a chance of thunderstorms in the afternoon. Waves 1 to 3 feet.
  Tonight: South winds around 10 knots, becoming southeast. Showers with a chance of thunderstorms in the evening, then showers with a slight chance of thunderstorms overnight. Waves 1 to 2 feet.
  Wednesday: Southeast winds 5 to 10 knots, becoming east. Showers in the morning, then showers likely in the afternoon. Waves 1 to 2 feet.
  Wednesday Night: Northeast winds 10 knots or less, becoming north. Showers likely. Waves 1 foot or less.
LAKE GAGE: water 73F, level 95.51 ft (normal)
MODEL SPREAD (where forecasts diverge):
  2026-07-28: highs [GFS 87, Euro 81, ICON 82] spread 6F; precip chance [GFS 60%, Euro 99%, ICON 80%]
  2026-07-29: highs [GFS 75, Euro 72, ICON 72] spread 3F; precip chance [GFS 70%, Euro 87%, ICON 83%]
  2026-07-30: highs [GFS 65, Euro 71, ICON 71] spread 6F; precip chance [GFS 54%, Euro 55%, ICON 65%]
AIR: AQI 52 Moderate (PM2.5) — Expect moderate levels of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in Vermont on Tuesday, July 28th.
SUN: rise 2026-07-28T05:35-04:00, set 2026-07-28T20:22-04:00, UV max 6.6
WEATHER UNDERGROUND / WEATHER.COM:
  high 81, low 66: Showers and thunderstorms late. Highs in the low 80s and lows in the mid 60s.
  high 74, low 63: Cloudy with rain. Highs in the mid 70s and lows in the low 60s.
WCAX METEOROLOGIST: Tuesday night and through Wednesday brings more steady rain shower activity that could be heavier at times, especially across southern Vermont. Rain amounts will be highly variable depending on where the heaviest downpours set up Tuesday and Wednesday. In general, the farther south you are, the more likely you are to see excessive rain. The farther north you are, the less likely you are to see a lot of rain. Totals will likely be enhanced in the central and southern Green Mountains, Adirondacks and communities on the southeastern slopes. The Upper Valley and I-91 corridor in southern Vermont could also see higher amounts.
